_note: Public funding-opportunity facts compiled 2026-11-10 for MW (docs/funding-follow-up-spec.md), rewritten 2026-11-10 to the Hub's writing rules with the facts unchanged. No people or matches: matches to real investigators are entered by MW in the live system. Confirm every date on the sponsor's page; rows with deadline null use deadline_text. Center-level rows come from the COBRE Administrator Handbook, chapter 19.

opportunities.name: American Heart Association Career Development Award
opportunities.sponsor: American Heart Association
opportunities.summary:
For investigators in the first years of an independent career.
The award is not open to anyone holding an NIH R01 or K99/R00.
Stroke research fits the award.

opportunities.name: PhRMA Foundation Faculty Starter Grant
opportunities.sponsor: PhRMA Foundation
opportunities.summary:
For early-career faculty at doctoral universities in the United States.
Check the scientific fit before applying.

opportunities.name: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Youth Violence Prevention Centers (RFA-CE-27-013)
opportunities.sponsor: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, National Center for Injury Prevention and Control
opportunities.summary:
The award funds a full research center, too large for one investigator to lead on this timeline.
Joining a team as a project lead is the usual way in.

opportunities.name: FRAXA Research Foundation Fellowship
opportunities.sponsor: FRAXA Research Foundation
opportunities.amount_text: $50,000 a year for up to 2 years
opportunities.summary:
The fellowship supports a named fellow in the principal investigator’s lab.
Treatment-oriented research is given priority.

opportunities.name: NIH R01, standard dates for new applications
opportunities.sponsor: National Institutes of Health
opportunities.amount_text: From a modular budget to an unrestricted budget
opportunities.summary:
Talk to the program officer before writing.
A single-principal-investigator R01 keeps eligibility for IDeA co-funding.

opportunities.name: Katz Early Stage Investigator R01 (PAR-25-322 and PAR-25-323)
opportunities.sponsor: National Institutes of Health
opportunities.summary:
For Early Stage Investigators starting a new research direction.
Preliminary data are not expected.

opportunities.name: Maximizing Investigators’ Research Award for Early Stage Investigators (R35)
opportunities.sponsor: National Institute of General Medical Sciences
opportunities.deadline_text: Check the NIH Guide (the COBRE handbook lists PAR-26-121)
opportunities.summary:
The award counts as an R01 equivalent and can receive IDeA co-funding.
The research must be basic science within the institute’s mission.

opportunities.name: Bioengineering Research Grants R01 (PAR-27-072)
opportunities.sponsor: National Institutes of Health (several institutes, including the National Institute of Biomedical Imaging and Bioengineering, the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke, and the National Institute of Child Health and Human Development)
opportunities.summary:
For projects driven by engineering.
The National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke joined the announcement in August 2026.

opportunities.name: National Center for Medical Rehabilitation Research Early Career Research Award (R03)
opportunities.sponsor: National Institute of Child Health and Human Development
opportunities.deadline_text: The listed dates ended October 16, 2026, so watch for a reissue
opportunities.summary:
The award builds data toward an R01 and keeps Early Stage Investigator status.
The project must include physical rehabilitation.

opportunities.name: Trailblazer R21 for New and Early Stage Investigators
opportunities.sponsor: National Institute of Biomedical Imaging and Bioengineering
opportunities.deadline_text: Check for a reissue (the last announcement was PA-25-169)
opportunities.summary: The award keeps Early Stage Investigator status unless the project moves to an R33 phase.

opportunities.name: Brain & Behavior Research Foundation Young Investigator Grant
opportunities.sponsor: Brain & Behavior Research Foundation
opportunities.amount_text: $35,000 a year for up to 2 years
opportunities.summary:
The research must relate to a psychiatric disorder, and anxiety and autism both count.
The foundation pays no indirect costs.

opportunities.name: Whitehall Foundation Research Grant and Grant-in-Aid
opportunities.sponsor: Whitehall Foundation
opportunities.amount_text: $100,000 a year for 2 to 3 years, or a $30,000 grant-in-aid
opportunities.deadline_text: The spring 2027 letter of intent closed October 1, 2026, so plan for the next cycle
opportunities.summary:
For assistant professors with about $200,000 a year or less in other funding.
Frame the project as basic neurobiology.

opportunities.name: Department of Defense Traumatic Brain Injury and Psychological Health Research Program
opportunities.sponsor: Department of Defense, Congressionally Directed Medical Research Programs
opportunities.deadline_text: The fiscal year 2026 deadline passed October 15, 2026, so watch for fiscal year 2027
opportunities.summary:
Some mechanisms are open at any career stage.
Clinical relevance is emphasized.

opportunities.name: Department of Defense Autism Research Program (Career Development Award and Idea Development Award)
opportunities.sponsor: Department of Defense, Congressionally Directed Medical Research Programs
opportunities.amount_text: About 3 Idea Development Awards, $2.25 million in total
opportunities.deadline_text: The fiscal year 2026 deadline passed October 22, 2026, so watch for fiscal year 2027
opportunities.summary: The Career Development Award excludes anyone with an earlier federal career development award.

opportunities.name: Parkinson’s Foundation Impact Award
opportunities.sponsor: Parkinson’s Foundation
opportunities.amount_text: $200,000 for 2 years, with indirect costs of 10% or less
opportunities.deadline_text: The 2026 letter of intent closed, and the next cycle opens in fall 2027
opportunities.summary: Researchers new to Parkinson’s disease should partner with an established Parkinson’s researcher.

opportunities.name: Parkinson’s Foundation Stanley Fahn Junior Faculty Award
opportunities.sponsor: Parkinson’s Foundation
opportunities.deadline_text: Open in the 2026 to 2027 cycle, so check the date
opportunities.summary: The award is offered every other year.

opportunities.name: BrightFocus Foundation Alzheimer’s Disease Research Standard Award
opportunities.sponsor: BrightFocus Foundation
opportunities.deadline_text: The 2026 deadline of September 1 passed, and the next is about September 2027
opportunities.summary: The early-career track is for researchers within 15 years of their degree who hold an independent position.

opportunities.name: Alzheimer’s Association Research Grant
opportunities.sponsor: Alzheimer’s Association
opportunities.summary: Check the current cycle’s eligibility rules on the association’s page.

opportunities.name: Foundation for Physical Therapy Research grants
opportunities.sponsor: Foundation for Physical Therapy Research
opportunities.summary:
For early-career physical therapy researchers.
The grants are smaller than a CNAP pilot but well regarded.

opportunities.name: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention R01: Preventing Interpersonal Violence and Suicide, Ages 10 to 24
opportunities.sponsor: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, National Center for Injury Prevention and Control
opportunities.deadline_text: Closed July 1, 2026, and a 2027 cycle is expected
opportunities.summary:
Youth violence is a named priority.
The sponsor is the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, not NIH, so confirm with the program officer whether the award counts toward the milestone.

opportunities.name: Youth Violence Prevention Interventions R01 (RFA-MD-24-002)
opportunities.sponsor: National Institute on Minority Health and Health Disparities
opportunities.deadline_text: Check whether the announcement is still active
opportunities.summary:
The announcement names bullying and cyberbullying.
It was updated in March 2025 to reflect new priorities.

opportunities.name: National Institute of Justice Research and Evaluation on School Safety
opportunities.sponsor: Department of Justice, National Institute of Justice
opportunities.deadline_text: The 2026 deadline was June 3, so watch for 2027
opportunities.summary: For research on the factors that affect violence in kindergarten through 12th-grade schools.

opportunities.name: Harry Frank Guggenheim Distinguished Scholar Award
opportunities.sponsor: Harry Frank Guggenheim Foundation
opportunities.summary:
For research on violence and aggression.
Reviewers’ feedback from an earlier application can shape a resubmission.

opportunities.name: Support for Research Excellence (SuRE) R16 (PAR-24-144) and SuRE-First R16 (PAR-24-145)
opportunities.sponsor: National Institute of General Medical Sciences
opportunities.summary:
The institution must receive limited NIH funding.
SuRE-First is for investigators with no earlier independent external grant.

opportunities.name: Institutional Development Award (IDeA) co-funding
opportunities.sponsor: National Institute of General Medical Sciences
opportunities.amount_text: Up to $350,000 in total costs for the first 2 years
opportunities.deadline_text: Ongoing, for the 3 most recent council rounds
opportunities.summary:
IDeA co-funding can support a strong R01, R15, or R35 from an IDeA state that missed the payline.
Multiple-investigator applications are not eligible.
After a near-miss score, talk to the program officer assigned to the application.
opportunities.fuller_text:
The institute assigned to the application nominates it for co-funding.
The Institutional Development Award program can co-fund a strong R01, R15, or R35 from an IDeA state that missed the payline.
Co-funding covers up to $350,000 in total costs for the first 2 years.
Applications from the 3 most recent council rounds can be considered.
Multiple-investigator applications are not eligible.

opportunities.name: Building Research Environments in Sponsored Programs Administration and Development (PAR-24-268)
opportunities.sponsor: National Institute of General Medical Sciences
opportunities.summary: The award strengthens the research environment, sponsored programs, and pilot-project programs at institutions with limited resources.

opportunities.name: Shared Instrumentation (PAR-24-265) and High-End Instrumentation (PAR-24-264)
opportunities.sponsor: National Institutes of Health
opportunities.amount_text: At least $25,000 for shared instruments, and $75,000 to $2 million for high-end instruments
opportunities.summary:
The awards buy shared equipment, such as a transcranial magnetic stimulation or near-infrared spectroscopy facility.
The version for institutions with limited resources (PAR-27-067) closed July 2, 2026.

opportunities.name: Administrative Supplements (PA-26-001)
opportunities.sponsor: National Institute of General Medical Sciences
opportunities.summary: The institute announces eligible areas through its Highlighted Topics, not through notices of special interest.
